raw: {"analysis": "Both responses provide comprehensive plans addressing the key requirements: byte-stable output verification, test coverage, downstream impact, rollback, CI cost, and flaky test handling. RGD is slightly stronger because it explicitly asks for clarification on the definition of 'byte-for-byte' (hash algorithm) and performance variance tolerance, which are critical to avoid ambiguity and follow-up questions. It also includes a more detailed rollback trigger (error rate >0.1% or cache miss spike >5%) and a post-mortem step, while PGD's rollback criteria are similar but less explicit. RGD's structured gates and cost-control measures are equally thorough, but the proactive clarification request makes it more actionable for the requester.", "verdict": "RGD"}
